thread_analysis.thread_summary: [COMPANY] (a first-time Bluetooth SIG registrant) works through quoting and registration for a single representative model, generating extensive field-by-field guidance on filling out the quote-request form, a clarification on the time-bound nature of free derivative-model registration (tied to the referenced module's Core Spec version remaining valid), and guidance on how compliance folder documentation scope depends on how many models are listed in the initial registration, including block-diagram detail-level flexibility. The thread closes with SIG approval and compliance folder shipment.
all_questions_found: Which Member Class should be selected on the quote-request form?
Should the device model name be written in Japanese, and can multiple models be listed together?
Are SW Version / HW Version mandatory fields on the quote-request form, even if not yet finalized?
Can the Product Description be a short, one-line Japanese description?
Which Product Category and Product Type should be selected?
Was checking 'request Allion to act as wire-transfer agent' for the Declaration Fee the correct choice?
Is there a time limit on how long free derivative-model registration remains available for models using the same module and host stack as an existing registration?
Once a derivative model is added to the Product List, can it continue to be sold indefinitely?
Are the required compliance folder documents (manual, block diagram, outline drawing) needed per individual model, or can they be shared across models?
How detailed does the product block diagram need to be -- can a generic, common-image diagram be used for similar-purpose devices?
After placing the order, does the customer need to provide or lend the registered device to the consultant?
thread_analysis.key_technical_discussion: The thread provides detailed field-by-field guidance for completing a Bluetooth SIG quote-request form (Member Class, model name formatting, SW/HW Version optionality at quote stage, Product Description brevity, Product Category/Type selection, and the Declaration Fee payment-method checkbox), explains that free derivative-model registration eligibility is tied to the referenced module's Core Spec version remaining valid (not indefinite), and clarifies that compliance folder documentation scope depends on how many models are listed in the initial registration's Product List, with block diagrams accepted at a generic, representative level of detail rather than requiring an exact circuit-level diagram per model.
thread_analysis.key_decision_logic: Quote-request form fields that are not yet finalized (such as SW/HW Version) do not need to be specified at the quoting stage and can be addressed later at actual registration time. Free derivative-model registration is available for as long as the referenced module's underlying Core Spec version has not been deprecated by Bluetooth SIG; models already added to the Product List before that deprecation date remain sellable indefinitely regardless of when the version is later deprecated. Compliance folder documentation scope is determined by how many models are listed in the initial registration: one representative model needs only that model's documents, while multiple models listed at initial registration each need their own documents; block diagrams are accepted at a generic, representative level of detail rather than requiring an exact, model-specific circuit diagram.
thread_analysis.risk_if_done_wrong: Treating quote-stage fields like SW/HW Version as mandatory before they are finalized could stall the quoting process unnecessarily. Assuming free derivative-model registration is available indefinitely, without checking the referenced module's Core Spec version deprecation timeline, could lead a customer to miss the free-addition window for future variants. Assuming every model in a multi-model initial registration can share one set of compliance folder documents, or insisting on an overly detailed block diagram, could lead to either an incomplete compliance folder or unnecessary extra work.
thread_analysis.consulting_takeaway: When guiding a first-time customer through the quote-request form, clarify which fields are genuinely required at the quoting stage versus deferrable to registration time. When discussing the free derivative-model addition feature, proactively flag that it is tied to the referenced module's Core Spec version deprecation timeline rather than being indefinitely available, since this affects long-term product-line planning. For compliance folder scope, clarify upfront how many models will be listed in the initial registration, since that determines how much documentation is needed, and reassure customers that block diagrams can be generic/representative rather than highly detailed.
